hook.text: On the disk, a program is just a file. It does nothing. It is passive.

alive.text: Run it, and it becomes a process: a program in execution. Active, with its own memory and its own state.

layout.text: Its memory has four parts. Text holds the code. Data holds the global variables.

layout2.text: The heap grows up when the program asks for memory. The stack grows down with every function call.

many.text: One program can be several processes at once, like two windows of the same browser.

life.text: Now follow one process through its life.

new.text: It is born in the new state. Once admitted, it moves to ready, and waits in line for a CPU.

run.text: The scheduler dispatches it. Now it is running.

intr.text: A timer interrupt stops it. Back to ready.

io.text: Dispatched again, it asks the disk for data. Now it is waiting. It could not use the CPU anyway.

trapQ.text: The disk finishes. Does the process jump straight back onto the CPU?

trapA.text: No. Waiting goes to ready, never straight to running. Only the scheduler moves a process from ready to running.

exit.text: At last it calls exit, and terminates. Five states, six arrows.

pcb.text: To pause a process and resume it later, the OS keeps a process control block for it: its state, its I D, its program counter, its registers, and more.

cs.text: A context switch saves the running process into its P C B, and loads the next one from its own.

cs2.text: During the switch, no useful work gets done. It is pure overhead.

fork.text: How is a new process born? With fork. fork makes a copy of the calling process, and both carry on from the same point.

ret.text: The only difference is the return value. The parent gets the child's P I D. The child gets zero.

exec.text: Then exec replaces the child's program with a new one, like ls. Same process, new code.

pow.text: If every process calls fork three times in a row, you get two to the power three: eight processes.

ipc.text: Processes can also talk: through a shared memory area, or by sending messages through the kernel.

ex1.text: A program is passive, a process is active.

ex3.text: Waiting never goes straight to running.

ex4.text: The P C B saves a process; switching is overhead.

ex5.text: fork returns zero to the child, the P I D to the parent.
